title: Canon of Scripture
definition: The canon of Scripture is the complete collection of books that God has given as His written Word for His people.
summary: The church did not create Scripture's authority; God did. The church recognized the books that were inspired by God and received them as Scripture. The canon identifies the books that belong in the Bible and serve as the standard for faith and practice.
christFocus: From Genesis to Revelation, the canon tells one unified story of redemption centered on Jesus Christ. The Old Testament prepares the way for Christ, and the New Testament reveals His life, death, resurrection, and kingdom.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: God gave His people a complete written revelation. Believers are called to receive the Scriptures God has provided rather than adding to or subtracting from His Word.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: A settled canon protects the church from false teachings, counterfeit revelations, and confusion about spiritual authority.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Read the whole Bible as God's unified revelation. Build your faith on the Scriptures rather than speculative writings, private revelations, or human traditions.
